content.content:
The detail panel presents a path entry in the Content section as a visible link rather than as bare text. Where a node's content.ref is a list of repo-relative paths, the paths the section shows are the entries rptlovpt makes activatable (rptlovpt), and each of those entries is drawn so that a reader can see it is something to be activated, set apart from the characters of the block that are not entries, instead of standing as text that merely happens to record a file's location. Being visible is the whole of the commitment: the entry's own appearance says from the block itself that the path can be activated, rather than leaving the reader to find that out by trying.

The entry's text is the path the block already shows, and this decision adds nothing to it: no file name in place of the path, no directory summary, no label, no quoted title, no icon or "open" control beside it, no truncation and no reformatting. The monospaced block therefore keeps showing the content type together with the paths that value gives, in the order it gives them, and the panel and the node's ref list cannot disagree about which files the body lives in (qwzwpxws). Nor does this decision add an element to the block: only the look of the entry that is already there.

This is a decision about appearance and nothing else. What the Content section shows is qwzwpxws's, and what a path entry is, and what activating one does, are rptlovpt's (rptlovpt, qwzwpxws); neither is restated, narrowed or extended here. The link is the look of an entry that was already activatable: it is not a second activation, not an extra input, not a variant of the one recorded, and it changes nothing about what any input does or where it leads, so an entry presented this way is reached and invoked exactly as rptlovpt records. Nothing here presents as activatable anything that rptlovpt does not make an entry.

The link belongs to those path entries and to nothing else in the section. The content type shown beside the paths names the type and is not a path and not an entry, so it is not presented as a link (rptlovpt, qwzwpxws); the block, the section's label, the value's frame and the other sections keep the presentation qwzwpxws gives them; and a path mentioned anywhere else — inside the selected node's kind, content or rationale text, or elsewhere in the panel — gains nothing from this decision. Every path entry on every value of that form is presented this way, whatever its content type, because qwzwpxws presents that form in one block for every type and rptlovpt makes every path in it an entry.

The look stops at being a link. This decision does not say which colour role an entry takes, whether a pointer cursor is shown over it, what happens to the entry on hover, what marks it while it has focus, which element carries the look, or which class vocabulary names it: each of those is a separate commitment with its own check, and none of them is fixed, required, forbidden or implied here. Nor does this decision add any class, style property or stylesheet rule itself. It states that the entry is presented as a link; the parts of that presentation are settled where they are owned.

A path that names no file is left where rptlovpt left it: rptlovpt states nothing for such a path and this decision takes it up no further. Nothing here settles how such a path is presented, and nothing here requires or forbids that it read like a path entry that names a file. Nor does anything here withhold a path, replace one, reorder the block's paths, duplicate the paths in a second surface, present them outside that section, or introduce a body for a node whose body lives in the referenced files (qwzwpxws).
content.rationale:
rptlovpt made each path in the Content section's path form an activatable entry and then stopped at the entry's focusability, leaving how an entry is drawn to the appearance decisions that own it, so as things stand the panel holds a control whose look says nothing about it: an entry that can be activated reads exactly like the inert text beside it in the same block, and a reader who has just been told the body lives in a named file has to try a path-shaped run of characters on the chance that it responds, or tab into the panel and hope. The affordance is the missing half of an activation that exists, and a link look is its smallest form — no element, no text, no behaviour, only the entry's own appearance carrying the fact that the path can be activated. That is also why this decision is the right place to stop: it fills exactly what rptlovpt left unstated and decides none of what rptlovpt settled, so activation keeps its one outcome and its inputs, and qwzwpxws's value keeps its type, its paths, their order and its frame.

The link's text stays the path the block already shows, because the section's job is to say where the body lives (qwzwpxws) and a path is the only name that carries from the panel to the file. A file name alone, a shortened path, a directory summary or an "open" control beside the entry would put the panel's rendering of the file where the node's own ref list belongs, and would leave the reader comparing a prettified entry against the path the node records. Keeping the characters and adding only the look keeps one account of the path across the node, the block and the activation.

Stopping at the existence of the look is what lets the rest be decided at all. The colour role the entry takes, the pointer cursor over it, the hover treatment, the focus outline and the class vocabulary are stylesheet facts a reviewer can point at in the styles, so each is checkable on its own terms and belongs to the decision that owns it; settled here, they would either be restated by those decisions or contradicted by them, and the distinction between an entry that reads as a link and whatever draws the link would be lost. rptlovpt took the same care from the other side — it added no class, no style rule, no hover cue and no focus indicator, and handed drawing to the appearance decisions — so this is one of those decisions, and it takes only the one part it owns rather than the entry's whole presentation.

Decidability at review time comes from the one thing this decision does fix: the appearance of the entry in its rest state says that the path can be activated. A reviewer can name the refuting observation without inventing a rule — a path entry drawn indistinguishably from the block's non-entry characters, so that the panel gives no appearance signal that the path is something to activate. What this decision leaves open is not what a link is made of but which of the recorded means of drawing one a given entry uses, and that is the question the neighbouring appearance decisions each answer on their own terms.
